Manchester (2004)  

Toxteth Street by MBLA Architects + Urbanists  

Manchester City Council commissioned the Firm to formulate a strategy for this region of East Manchester, which comprises a dense collection of pre-1919 terraced housing. Originally there was a mixed tenancy of private and council housing association ownership. A strategy was developed with a view to embracing the existing rhythm of the terraces, wherein roughly half the building stock would be preserved. Newly constructed linear housing would complement the existing stock, which acted as an “anchor” in formal terms, but also allowed for substantial tenant and owner selection. The criteria for the project were to ensure equivalency between the various tenures in terms of private and public amenity and to ensure that the neighbourhood, whilst being enhanced, maintained a homogenous quality.

When you are in the game menus selecting your teams and settings the background music is as if you were about to watch a Monday night football game (which I enjoy). Madden NFL 2013 Rating  

Gameplay 8/10 The running game is significantly enhanced and the passing game is still excellent. With the infinity engine enhancement this game can literally be played for hours.  

Graphics 9/10 The visuals in this game are the best for sports simulation games to date.  

Music 7/10 The soundtracks in this Madden are more concentrated on traditional football rather than contemporary hip hop and rock melodies. Like I mentioned before a mixture of both would be optimal.

perturbations.c: I already mentioned how the running game made a significant enhancement and there are observable distinctions in the passing game as well. There used to be several plays in every playbook that devoted Madden players could discover and utilize for automatic first downs, automatic touchdowns, or simple 2-point conversions. I attempted those same plays on every team and observed that they only function about 50-60% of the time if the play is performed perfectly. This is a wonderful improvement because it will persuade those who go for it on every 4th down to hesitate and consider the punt or field goal. Same applies for the automatic 2-point conversions that can easily provide an unjust advantage to someone competing against a friend. Every year Madden becomes more and more authentic and this year doesn’t let down.

Chicken Thokh  

Well, I ultimately recovered from the dreadful strep throat that tormented me for over a week... and the most dreadful thing was that I can't consume because it just hurt too much to swallow... (you know I am truly ill when I can't consume... coz there are only very few things in this world that would stop me from consuming... I ate when I got my wisdom tooth extracted!) I made chicken broth when I ultimately felt better but I contemplated - what a waste to discard the leftover chicken!! But it's so tasteless to eat it alone... thank goodness for the chicken thokh my mom used to prepare...   

based on my very limited Burmese lexicon, "thokh" is simply the Burmese term for "blend"... I grew up eating Burmese cuisine... mohinga, ohn-no klao swe, lehpat thokh, curry, etc. - just to name a few of my favorites! it's definitely an acquired flavor but I have grown to adore it... my impression of Burmese cuisine is that it's inexpensive, delightful, but takes a lot time (and effort to prepare). Some dishes are easier than others and to be frank, I am really not proficient at preparing them... but I do yearn for them from time to time... individuals may ponder what do Burmese individuals consume, it is such a impoverished nation... but let me inform you... the nation may be impoverished but their cuisine is not... perhaps next year, I can go and indulge my palate :)  

1 deboned, pulled meat from a cooked cornish game hen (you can replace with shrimp)  
1 cucumber or 2 small pickles, finely pulled  
1 cup cilantro, coarsely sliced  
1/2 purple onion, thinly chopped  
2 tbsp fried chopped garlic  
2 tbsp fried chopped shallots  
1 tbsp raw soy powder (豆粉)  
1/2 lime  
fish sauce, salt, pepper, MSG to flavor  

(optional) red peppers flakes, diced thai peppers, tamarind sauce, and cooked bean sprouts  

1. Heat 1 tbsp oil in the wok over high heat, add the pulled chicken, salt, pepper, MSG and combine (the chicken is tasteless since I utilized it to make broth). Reduce heat, add the soy powder, and toss.  
2. If you don't like the flavor of raw onions, toss the onions in the wok and cook till translucent  
3. Turn off heat and toss in the remaining vegetables, garlic / shallots. Add fish sauce and more salt and pepper to flavor. If desired, you can also add red peppers flakes / diced thai peppers / tamarind sauce / cooked bean sprouts.  
4. Squeeze the juice from a lime to #3 just before serving. Best served over rice.  

The key to good Burmese cooking (if you ask my mom) is taste as you season, which I agree fully, and mixing everything by hand... I have to state, there is the time and occasion where I find hand mixing enjoyable... (and it does taste better...) I just didn't do it this time... LOL  

Ya... prep work can be a nightmare over this one... but I ultimately found some shortcuts :) Instead of chopping and frying my own garlic and shallots, I found this! Makes life so much simpler! I actually purchased this in Taiwan but I am sure you can find it in an Asian grocery store :)

Overclocking & BIOS

Upon entering the EX58-UD4P BIOS everything appears the same as with any recent Gigabyte boards. The MB Intelligent Tweaker (M.I.T.) is the menu of selection for overclockers.

Before we move to the overclocking outcomes, there were two concerns we noticed when working with this BIOS. First and foremost the BIOS was very sluggish, making it somewhat irritating to navigate. This is an issue we have not encountered before when testing Gigabyte motherboards, so we are hoping a simple update will rectify the problem.

The second equally troublesome issue was the incapacity to manage BIOS profiles/configurations, which can be very frustrating when trying to overclock. These days it is just assumed that any motherboard costing over $250 will furnish you with that kind of capability. Again this is something we hope Gigabyte can remedy in a future update.

Now, once in the MB Intelligent Tweaker menu we were able to reach a 4.0GHz overclock using a Core i7 965 Extreme Edition processor (from the original 3.20GHz). We set the CPU Clock Ratio to 26x and elevated the BCLK Frequency to 154Mhz. The DRAM frequency was amplified to 1543MHz, while the QPI frequency was slightly overclocked to 7.4GHz. Finally the CPU voltage was augmented to 1.40v, which we deemed to be safe enough.

Because we were operating the memory above specification, the DRAM voltage was heightened to 1.64v, which is the highest recommended setting; going higher could damage the processor, we've been told. All other BIOS settings were left unchanged, meaning a total of six settings were modified in order to achieve this impressive overclock.

Pushing the Core i7 965 Extreme Edition processor past 4.0GHz was challenging, and each time we attempted we were met with numerous stability problems. This seems to be the limit of our processor, at least when using an air-cooler. Still, a 4.0GHz overclock on such a powerful processor is nothing to be ashamed about, as you will see once we begin benchtesting.

Kermit cloak on. Kermit cloak off. Kermit cloak on. Kermit cloak off. That's how today went.  

I don't mind that it drizzled periodically, I just wish I could interpret the weather. It seems that I would stroll for a long time with the Kermit cloak on, whipped by the almost constant breeze that skims these lands, and as soon as I opted to take it off that it would commence to rain again and I would have to fight against the wind to get the cloak back on over me and The Devil and buttoned up.  

In general, individuals have been very envious of the Kermit Cloak. Not one person who has observed me wear it has been unable to stop and gaze as I walk by. I expect Kermit cloaks to be the next significant fashion trend in Europe this winter.  

Today was a beautiful, calm filled day of walking. The discomfort in my feet still present, accepted, not resisted.  

One step after the other, through open fields, some newly cultivated, others newly chopped and others newly seeded. Past more fields of corn. Past more war cemeteries. Through more small villages that are almost like daytime ghost towns, the cars are there but no one is to be seen, except for the dogs who never fail to let me know whose territory it is. I was glad that one giant Saint Bernard was securely in his own yard. His barking and repeated leaping forcefully against the metal gate frightened me. I had visuals of him jumping over the fence and knocking me straight onto my back with his two giant front paws and then...I love dogs. I do. But sometimes they are just a little bit frightening here. Unknown. Unpredictable.  

Today as I walked with a full and tranquil heart, I took time to notice the small things.  

The orange slugs that slither along the road and on the grassy verge.  

The small black cricket ambling quietly beneath the grass.  

The white butterfly that fluttered alongside me.  

The worm that wriggled and writhed its way along the rain damp bitumen.  

The gulls that cried out behind me as they soared over the cultivated field.  

The wildflowers; pink, yellow, white, purple dancing in the constant breeze. And the bumble bees that suckled their sweetness.  

The white wispy dome of the dried dandelion waiting for the perfect moment to shed what it no longer requires.  

This is why I walk.  

To see.  

To wonder.  

To be here in this world,  

a bride married to astonishment.  

* When Death Comes by Mary Oliver

perturbations.a: Jackie Clune performs the title role in Phyllida Lloyd’s latest production of Julius Caesar, originally staged at the Donmar in late 2016 and now being released in cinemas. Building on a notable stage career, Clune was lured by Phyllida’s groundbreaking all-female Shakespeare trilogy that also includes Henry IV and The Tempest. While not the first staging of Lloyd’s Julius Caesar (the original staging having been presented in 2012) or Henry IV (2014), the play’s new venue in the Donmar’s pop-up theatre by Kings Cross gave new emphasis to the material in its effort to bring the marginalised narratives of female prisoners (the whole trilogy is performed as if being enacted within a women’s prison) into mainstream theatre. This production has now transitioned to the big screen in an effort to make it more reachable to a broader audience who by reason of location or financial circumstances, could not attend its initial performances in the theatre. We here at culturised had the opportunity to converse with Jackie just prior to the film’s premiere at this year’s Edinburgh International Film Festival where we discussed the gender dynamics of the production, its adaptation to the big screen, the prescient politics of the source material, and the prospects for women in the performing arts.

Saturday 6th July 2013  

Weather/Conditions: relentlessly foggy and soggy! Didn't see a thing and got a complete soaking. We walked through the center of a weather front...  
Distance/Ascent/Time: 21.7km / 1300m / c. 7h  
Accompanying: Liam  

It was a surprise to awaken and see the sun shining in the tent. Liam and I were camped beneath the Quoich dam, at the flat regions by the private road. The plan for the day was Gulvain, a solitary Munro by Fort William. Gairich was prominent above the campsite, bright and green in the sun. It was so easy just to unwind and feel on vacation for once.  

We packed up camp and headed south in the direction of Gulvain. I stopped by Spean Bridge to get hot rolls out of the Spar. By the time I was on the way to Fort William, the skies were turning grey and it was clear that bad weather was on it's way. By the time Liam and I were at the commencement of the route and ready to go, it was warm, humid and fine drizzle was spitting down.  

The craic with Liam was great, but the weather was pretty dreadful. That warm, moist stuff with low clinging mist to go. I hadn't been on Gulvain before, so it was a novelty to get a completely new Munro. You know you're close to completing them all when new terrain is a novelty!  

The approach up the glen was long and then we got started on the hill. Wind picked up, we went into mist, and then the rain fell heavier and heavier. We got high up as the weather got worse. It's a drag of a hill with a (probably) great view. So get it on a good day. For me, it was all about ticking one more off the list. The weather was incessantly wet, but not of the piss-take variety, at first.  

Then the skies dumped with water the way up to the summit cairn and back, and we headed down the way we came, every path now a stream, every hillside streaming water. On the way down, we startled some deer; they charged off and I saw (for the first time) one leap a clear twenty (or more?) feet across a burn. Utterly spectacular.  

The rain continued to fall on the way back out. The glen track was a long trek, for the future; it's best tackled with a bike (if you're me), or a quad bike (if you're Liam). we were completely drenched and my thighs were chaffing again as they had done in the first wet days of the Round. My gear was as soaked as it's been in a long time, and I headed back to Fort William to stay with James, driving down roads in the grey desolation of mist and drizzle pushed all the way down to sea level.  

All in all; a good day to get a single one ascended. Thank god I didn't go for the Mamores!

7 Principles for Wellness  

I attended the 2013 LDS Holistic Living Assembly this last weekend as a room facilitator--volunteer. I cherished the experience! I was able to be a facilitator for a few speakers. One of whom was Don Tolman. He travels all over the globe instructing about how to live healthily, without medicines, but with whole foods and wisdom. He believes in Self-care and self-education...not listening to government-imposed standards and regulations, but listening to your body and practicing judgment, and seeking God and the good in ways to enhance. He provided us a list of seven principles for good wellness.  

7 Principles of Wellness  

1. air - pure, fresh, flowing air becomes electrified which your body can then utilize to grant us energy. Take deep inhalations in the nose, emptying out the abdomen and then exhaled through the mouth.  
2. water - as a conductor of electric current it goes hand in hand with air. It is the fluid building block that constitutes 70% of our bodies. Each day, drink 1 qt for every 50lbs you weigh. It's excellent to consume a quart each morning first thing (with lemon juice) a half hour or more before you eat to activate your digestion.  
3. sunshine - just like flora and other living entities on this planet our bodies demand sunshine to flourish, develop, mend and rejuvenate. This provides you vitamin D and energy.  
4. movement - our Immune and Lymphatic systems which safeguard our bodies by cleansing our blood and cells are only activated by movement. Life should be activity. Don't remain still too long. take a pause every hour at least. And walk at least 30 minutes a day and minimal activity.  
5. whole foods - consume whole foods, minimally processed. These are non-processed. Steer clear of refined, hydrogenated and synthetic foods. If you can consume 60% fruits and vegetables a day, you're achieving well. Attempt to make it 80%!  
6. healthy connections - harmonious, loving connections in our personal, business and communal lives including with our pets are extremely vital. Take time to nurture those.  
7. passion - if you discover your passion you will cherish life more and you will be around to enjoy it longer! It grants us vibrancy and energy. If you don't know where to begin, get on your knees and pray for guidance. Then get to your feet and be okay reaching out to explore new paths. Everyone has something to contribute--find your passion and offering to give the world to be a better place.

It's excellent to consume a quart each morning first thing (with lemon juice) a half hour or more before you eat to activate your digestion.  
3. sunshine - just like plants and other living organisms on this land our bodies require sunshine to thrive, develop, repair and regenerate. This provides you vitamin D and energy.  
4. movement - our Immune and Lymphatic systems which defend our bodies by filtering our blood and cells are only activated by movement. Life should be motion. Don't remain still too long. take a break every hour at least. And walk at least 30 minutes a day and minimal movement.  
5. whole foods - consume whole foods, minimally processed. These are non-processed. Evade refined, hydrogenated and synthetic foods. If you can consume 60% fruits and vegetables a day, you're succeeding well. Try to make it 80%!  
6. healthy associations - harmonious, loving associations in our personal, business and community lives including with our pets are incredibly important. Take time to foster those.  
7. passion - if you find your passion you will love life more and you will be around to cherish it longer! It provides us vibrancy and energy. If you don't know where to start, get on your knees and pray for guidance. Then get to your feet and be okay reaching out to attempt new directions.
